extracted.intended_audience: Members of Congress, congressional staff, and policymakers overseeing federal competitive sourcing
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and shaping policy, procedures, and oversight for OMB Circular A-76 public-private (competitive sourcing) competitions, with attention to the Walter Reed A-76 case and implications for future DOD competitions. Includes statutory provisions, procedural rules (PWS/MEO), cost-comparison requirements, and proposed congressional options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of OMB Circular A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines federal policy for determining whether recurring commercial activities should be performed by the private sector or federal employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to classify activities as commercial (subject to competition) or inherently governmental (not subject to competition); companion FAIR Act requires agencies to inventory commercial activities annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Act inventory requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Activities Inventory Reform (FAIR) Act of 1998 requires Federal agencies, on an annual basis, to prepare and submit inventories of their commercial activities performed by Federal employees to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventories support classification decisions and identification of activities potentially subject to A-76 competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of inherently governmental activity
rubrics_metrics.description: An inherently governmental activity is an activity that is so intimately related to the public interest as to mandate performance by government personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes activities that: (1) bind the United States to take or not take action by contract/policy/regulation/authorization/order; (2) determine, protect, and advance economic, political, territorial, property, or other interests by military or diplomatic action, civil or criminal judicial proceedings, contract management, or otherwise; (3) significantly affect the life, liberty, or property of private persons; or (4) exert ultimate control over the acquisition, use, or disposition of United States property, including establishing policies or procedures for the collection, control, or disbursement of appropriated and other federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial vs inherently governmental classification rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial activities are subject to competition, while inherently governmental activities are not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular describes factors and specific definitions to determine how activities are classified; classification ultimately depends on several factors and must be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Performance Work Statement (PWS) team develops a statement of the work to be performed that is used as the basis for the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency must ensure that both the government's bid proposal (MEO) and private sector contractor proposals reflect all of the functions and personnel called for in the PWS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Efficient Organization (MEO) development and status
rubrics_metrics.description: The MEO is developed by a team (federal employees and sometimes a private sector contractor) and represents a streamlined reorganization of personnel — the Government’s in-house organization to perform a commercial activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MEO is the basis for government costs entered on the Cost Comparison Form; it does not exist unless it wins the competition; when MEO wins, a letter of obligation implements the decision; when contractor wins, a contract is awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firewalled roles between PWS team and MEO
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules call for a 'firewall' that would prohibit all communication between members of the MEO and members serving on the Performance Work Statement (PWS) team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Firewall intended to ensure fairness in the competition by preventing cross-communication that could bias PWS development or the MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum cost differential requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 policy establishes a minimum cost differential: no activities can be converted unless there is a minimal cost differential of $10 million or 10%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MEO is required to show a savings of at least $10 million or 10% over the private sector contractor’s costs in order to win; established so Government will not convert for 'marginal estimated savings.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition timeframes (post-2003 Circular)
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised Circular established new deadlines for the completion of A-76 studies — 12 months for standard competitions, and 90 days for streamlined competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under prior rules DOD was limited by law to a 30-month time frame for competitions; the new timeframes also accompanied appointment of competitive sourcing officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of competitive sourcing officials
rubrics_metrics.description: New Circular required agencies to appoint competitive sourcing officials such as the Human Resource Advisor (HRA), Agency Tender Official (ATO), Performance Work Statement (PWS) Team Leader, Source Selection Authority (SSA), Contracting Officer (CO), and Competitive Sourcing Official (CSO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These roles are specified to manage and provide oversight of the competition process and selection decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to exempt DOD during declared war or mobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised A-76 Circular states: 'The Department of Defense Competitive Sourcing Official (without delegation) shall determine if this circular applies to the Department of Defense during times of declared war or military mobilization.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows DOD the option to opt-out of A-76 during wartime/mobilization to avoid destabilizing personnel shortages.

rubrics_metrics.name: AA A (Army Audit Agency) independent review/certification of MEO bid
rubrics_metrics.description: Army Audit Agency (AAA) independently reviewed and certified the MEO’s bid proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent audit/certification functions can be part of the verification and oversight of MEO cost estimates and bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: ATO protest rights / GAO protest ability for A-76 competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency Tender Officials (ATOs) may file protests with GAO in connection with A-76 competitions; ATOs may file protests on their own initiative or at the request of a majority of employees involved in the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative changes (e.g., Section 326 of H.R. 4200) modified protest rights; effective dates and GAO decisions (e.g., Alan King) affect when and how protests can be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit to 540-day (18 month) competition duration (proposed/legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: H.R. 5658 (House-passed FY2009 NDAA) contains Section 321 which would limit the conduct of A-76 competitions to 540 days (about 18 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory cap on competition length intended to reduce multi-year, destabilizing competitions like WRAMC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require single government-wide definition of 'inherently governmental' (legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: H.R. 5658 (House-passed FY2009 NDAA) includes a provision (Section 322) which would require the analysis and development of a single government-wide definition for the term 'inherently governmental function.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to standardize classification across agencies and reduce variation in determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare retirement and health insurance costs; require comparable contractor benefits (legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 322 (as described) requires that retirement costs be compared and that any potential retirement and health insurance benefits offered by potential contractors be comparable to current benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks to ensure apples-to-apples cost comparisons by including retirement/benefits impacts in cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not automatically require competition at end of performance period (legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 323 amends 10 U.S.C. 2461 by not requiring DOD to automatically conduct a public-private competition under OMB Circular A-76, or any other provision of law, at the end of a performance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes automatic triggers that would force competitions at contract expiration without other consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insourcing requirement / guidelines (legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 324 provides for the insourcing of certain new and contracted out functions, including requiring the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness to prescribe guidelines and procedures to ensure that federal employees are considered to perform work currently performed by contractors; special consideration granted to inherently governmental activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalizes consideration of converting contractor-performed work back to federal employees and sets guidance responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit OPM influence over DOD competitions (legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 325 limits the influence of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) over DOD’s conduct of public-private competitions or direct conversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusts interagency roles to give DOD more control in its competitive sourcing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand 'interested party' and employee bid protest rights (legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 326 amends the definition of who is an 'interested party' and grants bid protest rights to those employee representatives who are designated as the agent for the majority of affected employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadens standing and procedural rights for employee representatives in contesting competition outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller General expedited protest authority (legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3557 grants certain authority to the Comptroller General to expedite actions in protests of public-private competitions under Circular A-76, and grants other rights to interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to speed resolution of protests to reduce delay and uncertainty following competition decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require competition before conversion for activities with 10+ civilian employees (legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 327 amends the Office of Federal Procurement Policy Act by requiring that a public-private competition be conducted (for executive agency functions performed by 10 or more agency civilian employees) before any activities may be converted to performance by contractors, with certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places a threshold on conversions to ensure sufficient scale before exercising conversion authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit announcement/conduct of competitions at military medical facilities unless conditions met (legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1676 prohibits the announcement or conduct of any (A-76?) at military medical facilities, unless certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed specifically at preventing destabilizing competitions at medical treatment facilities without meeting safety/resourcing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to prohibit inclusion of health care and retirement costs in cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: One Congressional option is to prohibit the inclusion of health care and retirement costs from the A-76 cost comparison process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Would change the structure of cost comparisons and potentially alter competitive outcomes; presented as an option Congress may consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish rotating team of acquisition professionals as Agency Tender Officials (ATO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed option: establish a team of acquisition professionals to rotate service as Agency Tender Officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to improve acquisition expertise and fairness in competitions by rotating experienced acquisition professionals into ATO roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require reporting on status of ongoing A-76 competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed option for Congress: Require specific reporting on the status of ongoing A-76 competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Would increase transparency and congressional oversight to detect problems earlier (e.g., long duration, staffing impacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit numerical quotas for A-76 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed option: Prohibit the establishment of numerical quotas for A-76 studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to remove pressure to 'hit' study targets that might prioritize quantity over appropriateness of competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require enforcement of A-76 rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed option: Require enforcement of the A-76 rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses reports that rules were not fully enforced during the WRAMC competition; enforcement could mitigate procedural abuses or deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant federal employees the same rights as private sector contractors (option)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed option: Grant federal employees the same rights as private sector contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Would aim to level procedural and contractual rights between parties in competitions, potentially affecting appeals, access to data, or transition processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage alternatives to A-76 and consider cancellation of pre-2003 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed option: Encourage alternatives to A-76 (e.g., High Performing Organizations (HPOs), insourcing) or cancel outstanding competitions conducted under the pre-2003 Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested because pre-2003 competitions have taken many years and caused destabilizing personnel effects; alternatives may avoid costs and challenges associated with A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding / policy consideration: A-76 effects on staffing and management during wartime
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding: The A-76 process created a destabilizing effect on the ability to hire and retain qualified staff members to operate garrison functions; cost savings proved counterproductive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: Congress should consider options (regulatory relief, suspension, acceleration of BRAC, or exclusion during war) to avoid degrading mission-essential staffing during high operational demand.
